sample_unit: LDCT scans (2,199 patients) from NLST test cohort
models_evaluated: three end-to-end deep learning models predicting 6-year lung cancer risk from single LDCT

links.outcome: Whether aggregate AUC vs subgroup calibration and operating-point metrics reveal model performance differences
links.effect: Models had similar AUCs (year-1 0.91–0.95) but calibration varied by Lung-RADS category; under-predicted at highest-risk tier (11% predicted vs 22% observed), which aggregate metrics concealed.
links.quote: Calibration was good in aggregate but varied by category: the models over-predicted in the low-risk Lung-RADS tiers, were well calibrated at intermediate risk, and under-predicted in the high-risk tiers where workup is decided (11% predicted against 22% observed at the highest-risk tier).

links.outcome: Cancer capture and net benefit of end-to-end models versus Lung-RADS and PLCOm2012 on same data
links.effect: Stronger end-to-end models had at least on-par or higher cancer capture and greater net benefit than Lung-RADS; on baseline scans capture exceeded Lung-RADS by more than 25 percentage points.
links.quote: On cumulative-gains curves and decision-curve analysis, the stronger end-to-end models achieved at least on-par or higher cancer capture and greater net benefit than Lung-RADS, and the advantage was largest on baseline scans, where Lung-RADS has no prior CT for comparison, exceeding it by more than 25 percentage points in capture.

unlisted_practices: Evaluating end-to-end imaging risk models with operating-point metrics (Lorenz curves, decision-curve analysis) anchored to Lung-RADS
Combining deep learning risk scores with Lung-RADS categories to re-rank patients in benign tiers

screen.reason: The study proposes and evaluates a deployment-aligned validation framework (decision-curve analysis, calibration across Lung-RADS risk categories, and operating point selection) versus standard discrimination metrics (AUC) using NLST data for end-to-end lung cancer risk prediction models.

primary.practice: deployment-aligned evaluation and decision-curve analysis anchored to clinical risk categories
